extracted.intended_audience: chemical manufacturers, importers, distributors, label and SDS preparers, employers, and OSHA compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and wording standards for Hazard Communication Standard (HCS) Appendix C (labels) and Appendix D (SDS) updates to align with GHS Rev. 7, including specific precautionary statement text, storage/disposal instructions, Section 1 and 2 SDS content, and related conditional instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skin sensitization — include 'Take off contaminated clothing and' wording
rubrics_metrics.description: For skin sensitization (C.4.7), add the phrase 'Take off contaminated clothing and' before 'wash contaminated clothing before reuse' (aligns with Rev. 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA determined the phrase was inadvertently omitted in earlier revisions; no comments opposed the change; finalizing as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific target organ toxicity (single exposure) — 'If exposed or concerned'
rubrics_metrics.description: For specific target organ toxicity (single exposure) (C.4.11), change precautionary statement text from 'If exposed' to 'If exposed or concerned' to maintain consistency across C.4 and with Rev. 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No comments opposed this revision; finalized as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division 1.4 explosives — instructional note and firefighting wording
rubrics_metrics.description: For Division 1.4 explosives (C.4.14), change the instructional note wording to 'except for explosives of division 1.4 (compatibility group S) in transport packaging' and replace 'Fight fire with normal precautions from a reasonable distance' with 'Fight fire remotely due to the risk of explosion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended to clarify when note applies and to specify the explosion risk; aligns with Rev. 7; OSHA declined out-of-scope suggested rewordings that would alter the adopted GHS language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flammable gases — 'In case of leakage, eliminate all ignition sources' (delete 'if safe to do so')
rubrics_metrics.description: For flammable gases (C.4.15), revise the precautionary statement from 'Eliminate all ignition sources if safe to do so' to 'In case of leakage, eliminate all ignition sources', removing 'if safe to do so' and adding 'In case of leakage'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: stresses danger of leaks creating explosive atmospheres and avoids language that could discourage prompt action. OSHA considered comments about safety of entering hazardous areas but relied on other OSHA requirements and training (e.g., PSM, HAZWOPER) to prevent workers from placing themselves in danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type A self-reactive substances — advise against fighting fires
rubrics_metrics.description: For Type A self-reactive substances and mixtures (C.4.21), delete certain extinguishing-related statements and add: 'In case of fire: Explosion risk. Evacuate area. DO NOT fight fire when fire reaches explosives.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA proposed these changes because it is dangerous to fight fires involving these materials; aligns with Rev. 7; no comments opposed these revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type B self-reactive substances — combine statements with conditional bracketed extinguishing instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: For Type B self-reactive substances and mixtures (C.4.21), combine existing precautionary statements and delete duplicate phrases; place 'Use . . . to extinguish' in brackets with a conditional note to include it only if water does not increase risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended not to alter meaning but to reduce duplication; aligns with Rev. 7; finalized as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organic peroxides — adopt Rev. 7 fire/explosion precautionary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: For organic peroxides (C.4.28), adopt Rev. 7 precautionary statements and firefighter instructions similar to those for self-reactive substances and mixtures, because their fire/explosion hazards are equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No comments opposed; finalized as proposed to align with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skin decontamination wording — 'Immerse in cool water or wrap in wet bandages' and variant for water-reactive gases
rubrics_metrics.description: For pyrophoric liquids (C.4.22) and solids (C.4.23) change 'immerse in cool water/wrap with wet bandages' to 'Immerse in cool water or wrap in wet bandages' (include both actions on label). For substances which in contact with water emit flammable gases (C.4.25) delete the wrap option and use 'Brush off loose particles from skin and immerse in cool water.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: clarify that both options should be listed for pyrophorics; for water-reactive chemicals, wrapping is insufficient because large volumes of water are needed; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage phrasing — use 'Store separately'
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace 'Store away from other materials' with the shorter 'Store separately' for self-reactive (C.4.21), self-heating (C.4.24), organic peroxides (C.4.28), and add 'Store separately' to Category 1 oxidizing liquids (C.4.26) and solids (C.4.27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA reasoned 'Store separately' is clearer and appropriate; aligns with Rev. 7; finalized as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move 'Store contents under...' instruction to prevention column
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete 'Store contents under . . .' from the storage column for pyrophoric liquids/solids (C.4.22/C.4.23) and instead place the instruction 'Handle and store contents under inert gas/ . . . ' (with similar instructional note) in the prevention column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: warnings about inert gas should apply to all handling (processing, storage, use), not just storage; aligns with UNSCEGHS recommendation and Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain air gap wording — include both 'stacks' and 'pallets'
rubrics_metrics.description: For self-heating substances and mixtures (C.4.24) change 'Maintain air gap between stacks/pallets' to 'Maintain air gap between stacks or pallets' to ensure labels include both words and not present them as a choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that preparers should include both terms on the label; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrosion-resistant container wording and conditional omission
rubrics_metrics.description: For corrosive-to-metals (C.4.29) change 'corrosive resistant/ . . . container with a resistant inner liner' to 'corrosion resistant/ . . . container with a resistant inner liner' (correct technical term) and insert a conditional instruction allowing omission if 'Keep only in original packaging' is included on the label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrects terminology and avoids redundancy; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify conditional instruction language about volatility and hazardous atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: For acute toxicity—inhalation (C.4.3) categories 1-3 and specific target organ toxicity (single exposure category 3) (C.4.11), revise conditional note from 'if product is volatile so as to generate hazardous atmosphere' to 'if the chemical is volatile and may generate a hazardous atmosphere.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor, non-substantive edits intended to improve clarity and align with wording used for flammable liquids (C.4.19); aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flammable liquids — applicability of 'Store in well-ventilated place. Keep cool' and Category 4 change
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that 'Store in a well-ventilated place. Keep cool' applies to Category 1 flammable liquids and other flammable liquids that are volatile and may generate an explosive atmosphere; delete 'Keep cool' for Category 4 flammable liquids (less volatile, flashpoint > 60°C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA's preliminary finding: 'Store in a well ventilated place' suffices for Category 4; change aligns with Rev. 7 and improves precision of precautionary instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explosives — specify applicable regulations content (labels) but limited to U.S. requirements for domestic labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: For explosives (C.4.14) clarify precautionary statements/instructions to store in accordance with local/regional/national/international regulations by requiring the label preparer to specify the content of the applicable regulations (OSHA interprets this to mean U.S. regulations for labeling intended for U.S. distribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA rejects commenters' concern that this would require listing every country's rules; for direct shipment to other countries a sealed shipping container may be labeled for the destination country; OSHA intends U.S.-focused labeling for domestic distribution and expects producers of hazardous materials to already be able to identify state/local differences when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage temperature scale — require Fahrenheit value (C.4 categories), Celsius optional
rubrics_metrics.description: For storage temperature statements (aerosols C.4.16, self-reactive C.4.21, self-heating C.4.24, organic peroxides C.4.28) require temperatures listed in Fahrenheit and allow Celsius in parentheses if the preparer chooses to include it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: other OSHA standards primarily use Fahrenheit; aligns with Rev. 7 recommendation that manufacturers use the region-appropriate scale but OSHA standardizes on Fahrenheit for U.S. labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional instructions for temperature-controlled materials
rubrics_metrics.description: For self-reactive substances/mixtures (C.4.21) and organic peroxides (C.4.28), add conditional instructions: (1) do not use 'store in a well-ventilated place' for temperature-controlled materials (condensation/freezing concerns); (2) include a storage temperature only if temperature control is required or deemed necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns Appendix C with Rev. 7; clarifies when ventilation/storage temperature statements are appropriate; no adverse comments received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal applicability — specify whether applies to contents, container, or both
rubrics_metrics.description: Add an instructional note in the disposal column indicating that the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor must specify whether disposal requirements apply to the contents, the container, or both (for relevant hazard classes in Appendix C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA finalized this to avoid ambiguous messaging that could put workers at risk; rejected commenter preference for more general statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explosives disposal — refer to supplier for disposal/recycling information
rubrics_metrics.description: For explosives (C.4.14) change the disposal precautionary note to read: 'Refer to manufacturer, importer, or distributor . . . for information on disposal, recovery, or recycling' and add an instructional note to specify the appropriate source of information in accordance with applicable regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: disposal of malfunctioning/unused explosives (e.g., fireworks, signal flares) may require specialist handling; supplier referral reduces unsafe disposal by unqualified parties; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSHA not adopting certain GHS Rev.7 conditional instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA declined to adopt a small number of Rev. 7 conditional instructions, including: (a) conditional omission of 'Avoid breathing dust/fume/gas/mist/vapors/spray' when 'Do not breathe ...' is used; (b) conditional omission of explosion-proof/static discharge precautionary statements where national/local legislation is more specific; (c) conditional omission for 'Protect from sunlight' for gases in transport cylinders per UN packing instruction P200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA concluded existing HCS rules (e.g., C.2.4) provide necessary flexibility or that U.S.-specific practices/packaging make the Rev. 7 conditional instructions inappropriate or unnecessary. OSHA received no comments opposing these non-adoptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix D introductory text — no required order within SDS sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a sentence to Appendix D clarifying that while each SDS section must contain all specified information, preparers are not required to present the information in any particular order within each section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to clarify existing practice and provide flexibility to SDS preparers; commenters supported this clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1 (Identification) — U.S. domestic address and telephone required
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1 of Table D.1 requires that the address and telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party listed on the SDS must be United States domestic contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA codified an existing requirement to reduce confusion for foreign suppliers and importers; importers are the responsible party for U.S. distribution and must use a U.S. address/phone on the SDS. OSHA rejected requests to make this optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 2 (Hazard(s) Identification) — include hazards from change in physical form and reaction products; classification required
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2 must present hazards associated with the chemical as shipped and: (a) hazards associated with a change in the chemical's physical form under normal conditions of use (aligned to paragraph (d)(1)(i)); and (b) hazards classified that result from chemical reaction products associated with known or reasonably anticipated uses (aligned to paragraph (d)(1)(ii)). Section 2(c) begins with 'Hazards classified under paragraph (d)(1)(ii) ...' to make clear manufacturers must classify these reaction hazards (not merely mention them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA revised Section 2 language to fully align with paragraph (d)(1) and to clarify that classification is required for reaction hazards. Related toxicity details belong in Section 11 and additional information may appear in Section 16. Comments by stakeholders were considered and addressed in these clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of substances formed during use — include in Sections 2 and 10, not required in Sections 3 or 8
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers are not required to list substances that form during use in Section 3 (composition) or Section 8 (exposure controls) if the hazardous substance is not present in its hazardous state in the mixture as shipped; however, OSHA expects information on substances formed by chemical reactions to be included in Section 2 and Section 10 (e.g., occupational exposure limits under Section 10(d): Conditions to Avoid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows OSHA's 2016 Letter of Interpretation and clarifies where downstream reaction-formed hazards should be documented on the SDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification principle — base on intrinsic properties, not anticipated exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Hazard classification must be based on the intrinsic properties of the chemical, including properties leading to hazards via physical form change or reaction products; classification is not based on anticipated workplace exposure levels except when a chemical is bound such that exposure cannot occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA rejected suggestions to relegate some reaction hazards to Section 16 where they might be downplayed; Section 2 exists to address hazards inherent to the chemical or reasonably anticipated uses.
